# Catalog search fixtures

`core-lexical-v1.json` contains a small shared corpus with explicit expected scores and normalized names. Catalog unit tests and PostgreSQL integration tests load the same cases; PostgreSQL fixtures create valid published listings and synchronized observations through their normal lifecycle helpers.

The cases cover exact identifiers, additive field weights without frequency boosts, whole-token matching, repeated terms, punctuation, Unicode letters/numbers and whitespace. Query-like punctuation is not interpreted as boolean, phrase or prefix syntax. Separate traversal tests compare complete results with pages of one and two records, including tied Unicode names on both local and indexed results. Expectations are fixed test data, not generated from the SQL implementation. This is a consistency regression corpus, not a relevance benchmark or a demo dataset.

Add a document only when an existing one cannot express the missing case. Each case names a zero-based document index, query and exact expected score; zero means no match unless the query is empty or whitespace-only browse. The ordering list is already in expected order, including ties, and supplies the expected normalized names. Use ASCII JSON escapes for non-ASCII characters. Confirm each expectation from the [search profile](../search_profile.go), not by copying the output under test.

Run `go test ./internal/catalog -run TestCoreLexicalSharedCorpus -shuffle=on -count=1` from the repository root for the scorer and memory traversal, then `make test-integration` for real PostgreSQL matching, composed pagination and repair gates. The SQL Unicode-class regression also guards the pinned Go Unicode tables; a changed toolchain mapping requires review and a new forward migration, not an edit to an applied migration. See the [search API conventions](../../../documentation/src/content/docs/reference/api-conventions.md#pagination-and-search-consistency) for client-visible behavior.
